title: The Japanese Occupation
subtitle: Six months to invasion, three years of occupation.
objectives: Describe the invasion and the fall of Bataan and Corregidor
Explain what the Second Republic was
Explain why resistance took the form it did

cards.title: The timetable stopped on 8 December 1941
cards.text: Japan invaded hours after Pearl Harbor. Within six months the islands were under occupation, and the plan for 1945 was gone.

cards.title: Bataan, then Corregidor
cards.text: The defence held longer than expected and still ended the same way.
points: **Manila was declared an open city** to spare it from bombing.
**Filipino and American forces** withdrew to the Bataan peninsula.
**Bataan surrendered in April 1942.**
**Corregidor held until May**, then fell too.

cards.title: What followed the surrender at Bataan
cards.text: Tens of thousands of prisoners were forced to walk roughly 100 kilometres north.
points: **They were already starving and sick** when they surrendered.
**Men who fell behind** were killed.
**Thousands died on the road**, most of them Filipino.
**It is remembered every April** as the Araw ng Kagitingan.

cards.title: Three years
cards.text: Tap each stop. December 1941 to February 1945, in five moments.

question.explain: Bataan fell in April 1942. Corregidor held out until May.

cards.title: Why the defenders ran out before they gave up
cards.text: Bataan was lost to supply, not to courage. A body without food stops working long before the will does.
points: **Rations were cut**, then cut again.
**Malaria and dysentery** spread through the lines.
**A starving soldier** cannot march or shoot straight.
**They surrendered sick**, which is why the march killed so many.

cards.title: Air power decided it early
cards.text: The campaign was shaped in the first two days, before most ground fighting began.
points: **Clark Field was hit** on 8 December, aircraft still on the ground.
**Without air cover**, supply by sea became impossible.
**Bataan could not be resupplied.**
**The defenders ran out of food** before they ran out of will.

cards.title: What people actually carried
cards.alt: A battered leather suitcase, a brass kerosene lamp, a dented tin canteen and a folded blanket on wooden floorboards
cards.text: A suitcase, a lamp, a canteen. Three years measured in what you could move.

cards.title: A government with a Filipino president and Japanese control
cards.text: Declared in 1943, with José P. Laurel as President.
points: **It had a constitution** and Filipino officials.
**Japan controlled** what it was allowed to decide.
**Most historians call it a puppet state.**
**Laurel argued** he took the post to shield Filipinos from worse.

question.text: The Second Philippine Republic was fully independent.
question.explain: It had Filipino officials and a constitution, but Japan controlled its decisions. It is generally described as a puppet state.

cards.title: Collaboration is the hardest question of the period
cards.text: Some who served under the occupation said they did it to protect people. Others took the chance.
points: **Judging it afterwards** divided the country for years.
**Laurel was charged**, then amnestied.
**There is no clean answer**, and historians still argue.
**Hold both facts:** the republic was controlled, and some who served meant well.

question.text: Who was President of the Second Republic?
question.explain: Laurel led the 1943 republic under Japanese control.

terms.def: A city declared undefended, to spare it from attack.
The forced march of prisoners after Bataan's surrender in 1942.
A government that appears independent but is controlled from outside.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Japan invaded in December 1941; Bataan fell in April 1942.
The Death March followed the surrender; thousands died.
The Second Republic of 1943 had Laurel as President and Japan in control.
Collaboration remains a genuinely contested question.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 3 Social Studies, the first of two weeks on the occupation. The campaign is explained causally rather than as a list of dates: air power lost in the first two days meant Bataan could not be resupplied, which is why a determined defence still ended in surrender. The Death March is stated plainly, with the distance and the outcome, and without detail that would serve no teaching purpose. The Second Republic is given its real complexity — a constitution and Filipino officials, with Japan deciding what they could decide — and collaboration is presented as genuinely contested rather than settled, because that is the honest position and he is old enough for it.
discussion: Why did losing aircraft on the ground decide so much?
What makes a state a puppet state?
Why do historians still argue about collaboration?
extension: Find out whether anyone in your family's province has a wartime story.
Look up why Araw ng Kagitingan is in April.
misconceptions: That the Second Republic was independent.
That collaboration has a simple answer.
